_readme: Vibe profiles for SIGNAL's station roster -- what each station actually
wants and doesn't, distilled from the rejection/correction history
scattered across program.js's comments (50+ passes of it) plus session
context that's already been lost from the file itself (the network-ops
dashboard's tracks: [] rewrite necessarily strips inline comments on
save -- see tools/network.html's own header comment).
`acceptedArtists` is mechanical and goes stale the moment the roster
changes -- treat it as a snapshot, not a source of truth; re-derive from
program.js directly (or regenerate this block) before relying on it.
`constraints` and `rejections` are the actual value here: qualitative
judgment calls that took real back-and-forth to establish and are NOT
recoverable from the current file alone. Update this by hand (or ask
Claude to) whenever a curation pass removes tracks with a stated
reason -- capture the reason here before it's gone.
Built 2026-08-23 (55th pass) as the first half of the pending-track-
queue feature for proposing new tracks -- this is what a suggestion gets

distortion-field.genre: 90s grunge and alternative rock -- the Seattle sound and its ripple effects
constraints: Stay in grunge/alt-rock proper -- guitars, raw vocals, radio-ready angst. Not pop-rock crossover, not post-grunge (2000s) unless it's genuinely of-era.

Rage Against the Machine was added 2026-08-29 at the curator's request and is the one artist here from outside grunge/alt-rock proper -- 1992, of-era, guitars and raw vocals, but rap-metal rather than Seattle or its ripple. A deliberate widening of the lane, not a precedent that the lane is open: this station has turned a candidate away on lane alone (Third Eye Blind, issue #27). Further rap-metal or crossover proposals still need their own argument.

rejections.reason: Passed on the LANE, not on quality or availability -- 2026-08-27, issue #27, the first outside suggestion this station has had. The candidate (gjdLAsnR_Ws) auditioned completely clean: right recording, embeddable, wide licence, "- Topic" upload, artist not already here. Nothing mechanical to hold against it. It falls to this station's own first constraint instead -- "not pop-rock crossover" -- because Semi-Charmed Life is about as far toward the bright, jangly, radio-pop end as the decade goes, dark subject matter notwithstanding, and 1997 San Francisco is a long ripple from an early-to-mid-90s Seattle lane. Next to Nirvana, Alice In Chains and Screaming Trees it would read as the odd one out. Recorded here because the call is arguable rather than obvious: the reporter was explicitly invited to argue that the constraint is drawn too tight, and if a later pass loosens it, THIS is the track that should be reconsidered first. Note also what the stated reason was -- "it's 90s rock, it's good" -- an argument for the decade rather than for this station, which is the distinction the suggestion form's first bullet asks for. Closed 2026-08-28: the invited counter-argument was not made, so issue #27 was closed as a pass with this reasoning attached rather than left open indefinitely. The door was left explicitly open to reopen and argue it.

Removed from the station on 2026-08-28 by the curator, on personal taste and preference -- not on availability, licence, embeddability or lane mechanics. Every one of these auditioned clean and had been argued for on its merits when it went on; several came from an outside suggestion pass. Recorded because a removal with no reason reads as an oversight and gets re-proposed: this one was a judgement call and needs no further justification than that, but re-proposing it needs a NEW argument rather than a re-check of the mechanics, which will pass again.

drift-mode.genre: Ambient, modern classical, and drone -- built for stillness
drift-mode.eraLane: no strict era; contemporary ambient/drone plus modern-classical-adjacent pieces
acceptedArtists: Brian Eno / Orchestra of the Swan
A Winged Victory for the Sullen
constraints: Modern-classical-ADJACENT ambient is welcome (Arnalds, O'Halloran, Einaudi are already on the roster) -- but a piece that reads as straightforwardly classical/neoclassical, rather than ambient-with-classical-texture, is the wrong lane for this station specifically.

OPEN QUESTION, found 2026-08-26: the neoclassical boundary below is not actually settled. Nils Frahm's "Says" is listed as rejected for being too straightforwardly classical, yet it is still on the roster, and Einaudi's "Nuvole Bianche" sits beside it while the constraint blesses Einaudi by name. Either the rejection was recorded and never acted on, or the line moved. Resolve it before leaning on the Richter/Frahm precedent to reject anything new -- and prefer unambiguous ambient/drone meanwhile, which is what the 2026-08-26 batch did to sidestep the question entirely.

Sourcing is easy here compared with the other stations: contemporary ambient and drone is well served by artist "- Topic" channels, and all six of the 2026-08-26 additions are Topic with no flags at all. The real hazard is length -- full-album streams dominate search results for this genre (43, 59, 66 and 185-minute uploads all surfaced), so check duration and take the single-track upload.

Length has a FLOOR as well as a ceiling, established 2026-08-29: Boards of Canada's 'Olson' auditioned clean and was left out at 1:32, under this station's own shortest track (2:33). The ceiling is generous -- Basinski 62:11 and Eno 55:04 are on the roster -- so the hazard really is full-album uploads, not long pieces. Also reject uploads marked (Excerpt): a part of a piece is not the piece.

rejections.reason: Read as classical/neoclassical proper rather than ambient -- too close to RELIC SIGNAL's retired all-classical lane. Source comment stripped by a later dashboard edit; captured from session context 2026-08-23.
Same call as the Richter track above -- too straightforwardly classical for this station's ambient/drone lane.

constraints: Strictly synth-driven new wave/synthpop of the era -- drum machines and cold hooks. Not later-80s pop-rock crossover, not synthwave (that's a modern retro genre and belongs on CIRCUIT CRUSH instead).

Japan was on acceptedArtists from the start with no track. Reason found 2026-08-29: 'Ghosts' has no official or Topic upload anywhere, only fan channels. The artist is on the station now via 'Quiet Life', which does. Do not spend another search on Ghosts unless an official upload appears.

midnight-neon.genre: tech house -- rolling basslines, chopped vocal hooks, and drops built for a big room
midnight-neon.eraLane: roughly 2018 onward, weighted heavily to the last three years; this is a current-rotation station, not an archive one
constraints: The lane deliberately spans BOTH ends of tech house: festival-scale (Dom Dolla, John Summit, FISHER, James Hype, Diplo, Chris Lake) and the Ibiza/underground end (Jamie Jones, Michael Bibi, PAWSA, Patrick Topping, Mochakk). Do not purify it toward either -- the mix is the format. The tagline says "underground" but the roster is honestly about half main stage, and that is intended.

Club versions are the format here, not an outlier. Durations run 2:26 to 6:44 and a six-minute mix is normal on this station in a way it is not anywhere else on the dial -- do not reject a track for length, and do not prefer a radio edit just because it is shorter.

Nearly every title here exists as BOTH an extended mix (typically 5-7 min) and a single edit (2:30-3:30). Either is acceptable, but check the duration so you know which one you actually took -- the titles frequently do not say, and re-upload channels mislabel them.

Vocal hooks are in-lane, not a compromise ("Beggin'", "Ferrari", "Where You Are", "You Give Me A Feeling"). This is not a purist instrumental station. What is out of lane: EDM/big-room, bass house, and progressive-trance crossover.

Channel provenance: prefer the artist's own channel, a label channel (Defected, Insomniac, Snatch!, Toolroom, CircoLoco, Hot Creations, Big Beat, Astralwerks, Experts Only, Dim Mak, Nervous), or a label-delivered "- Topic" art track. Tech house search results are DOMINATED by re-upload channels -- Myth of NYX, 7clouds, Top Hits USA, Selected., blanc, PROFOUND, Groove Bassment -- which often carry correct audio but have unverifiable provenance and unreliable mix labelling. CID's "Fancy $hit" was moved off one of these onto CID's own Topic delivery once a search found it; do the same rather than settling.

Trap specific to this genre: several of these artists' most-viewed uploads are FESTIVAL SETS, not tracks. A search for "Mochakk Jealous" returns his Circoloco Sonar set above the studio single, and Dom Dolla/Odd Mob/Cloonee all have live sets outranking their releases. Always confirm the result is the track, not an hour of one.

The festival-set trap above confirmed live 2026-08-29: searching 'FISHER Losing It' returns his Coachella 2019 set (6:36) directly beside the 4:09 studio audio. Duration is what separates them. Also note CamelPhat & Elderbrook's 'Cola' was taken at Aug 2017, five months before the stated 'roughly 2018 onward' line -- accepted on the 'roughly' and flagged in stations.js as the first to pull if that era boundary is meant strictly.
midnight-neon.notes: Roster built 2026-08-28 from a 30-title brief, replacing the temporary 60s-oldies test rotation that ran here 2026-08-25 to 2026-08-28. All 30 verified in one clean audition run (UNVERIFIED: 0), all embeddable, licence breadth 121-249 countries. Nearly all flagged UNKNOWN-CHANNEL at the time, which was correct and harmless: provenance is scored against the channels the station already used, and those were the oldies uploads this pass deleted. From the next pass onward it scores against the label/artist channels above, so the signal becomes meaningful again.

priorFormat.retired: MIDNIGHT NEON, late-night electric blues. Ran from the 60th pass (2026-08-24) until the SYNAPSE rename (2026-08-28). Do not propose against this; kept for the rejection history.
priorFormat.genre: late-night electric blues -- minor-key slow burns, lush horns, reverberant guitar solos
priorFormat.eraLane: no fixed decade; the first 28 tracks run 1947 -> 2012, weighted to classic electric blues
constraints: The brief is a mood, not a decade: dark highways and low-lit lounges after hours. Slow burns are welcome at length -- the roster already carries 7-9 minute cuts (Tin Pan Alley, If Trouble Was Money), so runtime is not a reason to reject.
Electric blues, not acoustic/Delta country blues -- the desc says electric and the whole station leans on amplified tone and reverb.

Sourcing differs from the guitar-rock stations: pre-1970 blues catalog has no official video, so artist "- Topic" channels (label-delivered Art Tracks) are the norm and are fine. Fan/compilation uploads are not -- all 28 are Topic, label, artist-official or VEVO.

Nearly every classic here has multiple near-identical Topic uploads across compilations. Check duration before picking: it is the only cheap way to catch a live take, a single edit or a modern rework (an EDM "rework" of a John Lee Hooker cut sits on his own Topic channel).

rejections.reason: Song collision -- Etta James already holds this song on the station. The artist is otherwise in-lane; a different track would be fine.

rejections.track: It Serves Me Right to Suffer
rejections.reason: Not a lane call -- dropped from the 2026-08-25 batch because its Topic uploads run 3:29 / 5:03 / 5:50 and none could be pinned to the album master without listening. Worth revisiting with a confirmed ID.

momentum.genre: Chillhop and instrumental beats for focus -- sampled jazz, lo-fi drums
momentum.eraLane: no strict era; instrumental hip-hop/downtempo/lo-fi beats scene, roughly 2000s-present
constraints: Meant to hold focus without breaking it -- "just enough melody," light and unobtrusive. Heavier/moodier downtempo or trip-hop proper is an adjacent but wrong-weight lane; keep it light.

rejections.reason: Reads as trip-hop/downtempo proper -- heavier lane than this station's lofi-chillhop winddown vibe. Source comment stripped by a later dashboard edit; captured from session context 2026-08-23.
Same call as Massive Attack above -- too heavy/moody for MOMENTUM's light focus vibe.

momentum.retired: Replaced by MIDNIGHT NEON (60th pass, 2026-08-24) -- same dial slot and glyph, new format. Kept for the rejection history below; do not propose against this profile.

city-lights.genre: Japanese city pop -- glossy production, funk basslines, Tokyo after dark
constraints: HARD RULE, explicit editorial decision 2026-08-20: Japanese artists only. Western yacht-rock/AOR that sounds similar (Steely Dan, Toto, etc.) does NOT belong here even though it's genre-adjacent -- this is specifically a Japan-only lane.
Verify original-artist credit carefully -- a song has been mis-credited to the wrong artist before (a listed "Casiio" cover turned out to actually be Yasuha's original).

Sourcing runs opposite to the guitar stations: most of this catalogue was never officially uploaded, so fan and archive channels carry roughly two thirds of the roster and are accepted here out of necessity. Prefer artist "- Topic", label channels (Victor, Sony Music (Japan), VAP, PANAM, MUSIC Liverary) and artist-official where they exist -- they are also the defence against the mis-credit rule above, since fan re-uploads are where covers get labelled as originals.

Check region-locking, not just oEmbed -- unique to this station. Japanese label uploads are commonly geo-fenced and an oEmbed 200 says nothing about it; confirm the video is US-available and embeddable before proposing. Watch for Night Tempo "Showa Groove" mixes (modern remixes), live cuts, and "Original Basic Track" uploads that are backing-track outtakes.

The mis-credit warning above earned itself three times in one pass (2026-08-29), all of them Topic uploads that look correct in a result list: 'AIRPORT LADY' on Ai Furihata - Topic is a cover, not Kadomatsu; 'Bomber' on Hirotaka Mori - Topic is not Yamashita; a Nanako Sato search returns 'Nanaco', a different artist. Read the CHANNEL, not the title. Related: Casiopea's Asayake has no clean upload of the 1979 original -- the available ones are 'Casiopea 3rd', the later lineup re-recording it.

circuit-crush.genre: Synthwave and retrowave -- arpeggios, gated drums, a drive that never ends
acceptedArtists: W O L F C L U B
constraints: Owns the darker/harder end of synthwave -- Perturbator, Carpenter Brut, GosT and similar belong here specifically, NOT on CIPHER, even though CIPHER is also electronic. This boundary has been deliberately enforced before (see CIPHER's rejections below).

Sourcing here is the EASIEST of any station (2026-08-29): artist '- Topic' channels plus the scene's own label channels (NewRetroWave, Aphasia Records, Mad Decent) meant all 19 candidates auditioned clean. GUNSHIP's 'Dark All Day' is the one known gap -- the only Topic upload is a Power Glove remix, the rest are fan re-uploads. Availability, not lane.

atomic.genre: In-universe atomic-age broadcast -- swing, jump blues, doo-wop
constraints: TIGHTEST constraint on the roster: not just "any genuine 40s/50s classic" -- must be verifiably a real track that actually plays on Fallout 4's Diamond City Radio or Fallout 76's Appalachia Radio. A track has been pulled before for being period-correct but NOT actually on those in-game stations (checked against the Fallout Wiki tracklists).

Attribution precision matters -- credit the actual original recording artist, not a more-famous cover (e.g. "Good Rocking Tonight" is Roy Brown's original, not the Wynonie Harris version some sources list).

Verified against a published Diamond City Radio tracklist on 2026-08-29 rather than from memory, which is the only way to satisfy the Fallout-canon rule above. A dozen further genuine gaps exist if this station is taken to 50 -- among them Ink Spots 'Maybe' and 'It's All Over but the Crying', Billie Holiday 'Easy Living', Roy Brown 'Mighty Mighty Man', Bob Crosby 'Dear Hearts and Gentle People' and 'Happy Times', Tex Beneke 'A Wonderful Guy', The Three Suns 'Worry Worry Worry', Connee Allen 'Rocket 69' (note the spelling, Connee not Connie), Betty Hutton 'He's a Demon He's a Devil He's a Doll', Frankie Carle 'One More Tomorrow', Cole Porter 'Anything Goes'. Several of those verified clean already.

rejections.track: Jump Jive An' Wail / Minnie the Moocher / Choo Choo Ch'Boogie / Boogie Woogie Bugle Boy (original selection)
rejections.reason: Genuine 40s/50s classics but not actually on Diamond City Radio or Appalachia Radio -- replaced with tracks verified against the real in-game tracklists (19th pass).

hackback.genre: Golden-age and underground hip-hop -- boom-bap, deep cuts
hackback.eraLane: primarily late 1980s-1990s golden age, some adjacent-era classics
constraints: Genuinely coast-to-coast -- NY is if anything the heavier side (Tribe/De La/Wu-Tang/Nas/Gang Starr/Pete Rock/Digable Planets/MF DOOM/Black Star) alongside West Coast (Dre/Ice Cube/Warren G/2Pac/Cypress Hill) and Outkast (Atlanta). A "west coast legends" framing was checked against the actual tracklist and found wrong (52nd pass) -- don't skew additions toward any one coast without checking the balance first.

Coast balance, measured 2026-08-25 rather than assumed: before this pass roughly half the roster was New York. The 8-track addition was weighted away from it on purpose (3 NY, plus New Jersey, Houston, Chicago, Oakland and Philadelphia). Re-measure before the next batch instead of trusting this number -- it is a snapshot, like acceptedArtists.

Before 2026-08-25 the station had no women across 21 artists. Queen Latifah is the first. Golden-age canon has plenty more (MC Lyte, Salt-N-Pepa, Lauryn Hill/Fugees, Roxanne Shante) and none are represented yet.

On the open question under the Snoop Dogg rejection -- whether this station steers away from radio-famous tracks toward deeper cuts -- the roster itself argues against it: C.R.E.A.M., Ms. Jackson, California Love, Regulate, Insane in the Brain and It Was A Good Day are all canon hits. Treat that removal as a taste call on the track until something else suggests otherwise.

Coast balance re-measured 2026-08-29 before the batch that took this station to 50: NY was 24/43 (56%). The seven added were 2 NY, 1 NJ, 3 West, 1 South, landing NY at 26/50 (52%). Re-measure again rather than trusting that number. Women went from 1 artist to 4 (Queen Latifah, Salt-N-Pepa, MC Lyte, Fugees); Roxanne Shante is the one named in the earlier gap note still not represented. Mobb Deep's Shook Ones Pt. II is verified clean (rTKpYJ80OVQ) and was passed over on coast alone.

rejections.reason: Removed in the 2026-08-23 curation pass. No stated reason was captured -- worth confirming whether this reflects a real boundary (e.g. steering away from more mainstream/radio-famous tracks in favor of deeper cuts) or was a one-off taste call, before treating it as a pattern.

cipher.genre: Big beat and breakbeat electronica -- late-night hacker-movie soundtrack energy
constraints: Big-beat/breakbeat energy specifically -- upbeat, propulsive, "hacker movie soundtrack." NOT the darker synthwave/electronic lane (that's CIRCUIT CRUSH's territory, enforced deliberately -- see its profile) and NOT moodier IDM/glitch (Aphex Twin has been rejected from this station twice, see below).

Audio-quality bar, not just genre fit: a track has been pulled purely for having dialogue/interview audio baked into the official video, even though the song itself fit ("Da Funk" precedent) -- check the actual video, not just that a clean studio version exists somewhere.

Photek is on this list but has NO track: Ni Ten Ichi Ryu has no official or Topic upload anywhere, only fan channels. Juno Reactor's Mona Lisa Overdrive is likewise unusable -- the 4:45 licensed cut is NARROW-LICENCE:18 and the only clean upload is the 10:09 album version. Both were wanted on 2026-08-29 and blocked on availability rather than lane; re-check if a wide-licence upload ever appears.

rejections.reason: Rejected once explicitly (34th pass, too IDM/experimental for this station's big-beat lane), accidentally re-added in a later pass without noticing the earlier rejection, caught by the network-ops dashboard's overlap checker, removed again in the 2026-08-23 curation pass. Treat Aphex Twin as firmly off-limits for this station going forward -- it's been tried and rejected twice now.
Same rejection as Windowlicker above, same pass.
Pulled alongside the Aphex Twin tracks in the same pass -- likely the same too-heavy/experimental call, though the exact reasoning for this specific track wasn't separately documented.
Not a genre rejection -- pulled because the official video's audio has dialogue/interview footage baked in, not a clean listen for a radio station.

Not a taste rejection -- blocked on availability, 2026-08-27 (issue #19). Proposed for the Matrix lane and it fits; there is simply no upload that clears the bar. The "- Topic" upload (61V3EsoNFUQ) is licensed in 6 countries, the exact trap the narrow-licence check exists for: the US is among the 6, so a US-only check passes it and it is dead air for almost everyone else. The official Prodigy channel carries only a live-in-Russia take (f0Olyr9zRto, 6:44), and every remaining hit is a fan re-upload. Re-check if a wide-licence studio upload ever appears -- this one is worth taking then.

constraints: Single-artist station by design -- 100% Nine Inch Nails. Do not propose other industrial/NIN-adjacent artists (Ministry, Skinny Puppy, etc.) without confirming first; this station's whole identity is being NIN's own dedicated frequency.

Channel provenance carries a LICENSING consequence here, found 2026-08-30. NIN's "- Topic" uploads from the With Teeth / Year Zero era are licensed in THREE countries; the same era's video-channel uploads are licensed in 249 (The Hand That Feeds on NineInchNailsVEVO, Survivalism on Rob Sheridan, NIN's longtime art director). Older Topic uploads are healthy -- The Fragile and Broken sit at 121 -- so this is that specific upload batch, not Topic in general. Confirmed on three separate Interscope-era Topic uploads (Right Where It Belongs, Zero Sum, Every Day Is Exactly The Same), all exactly 3. For that era prefer the video channels and check availableCountries.

The 3-country licence is INVISIBLE from the curator's chair, which is the whole reason this is written down: the US is inside that 3, so the track plays perfectly here and is dead for nearly everyone else. It was never catchable by the tooling of its own day -- the track went in 2026-08-25 13:18, audition.js was not written until 16:44 that afternoon, and the NARROW-LICENCE threshold landed a day after that. Nothing re-asked the question until check-roster.mjs was built on 2026-08-29 for exactly this, and its first deep probe of the roster found it. Never conclude a track is fine because it played, or because it passed on the day it was added.

Fan and archive channels are accepted here out of necessity and carry 7 of 29 tracks (Something I Can Never Have, Wish, The Perfect Drug, Into the Void, Somewhat Damaged, Sin, Reptile) -- used where no official upload exists. Right Where It Belongs is the standing case: no official video was ever made, so its only official upload is the 3-country Topic one and every wide-licence alternative is a fan re-upload. Prefer official where it exists; the trade is real, since a fan upload can vanish to a copyright claim where a Topic one will not, and check-roster.mjs is what catches that when it happens.

green-room.genre: No genre. The subject is the format.
green-room.eraLane: 1970 to now, deliberately unbounded -- Black Sabbath and Kacey Musgraves are on the same rotation.
constraints: The ONLY membership test is that the song is literally, lyrically about cannabis -- named, described, or the whole premise. Genre is not a constraint here and must not become one: doom metal, G-funk, roots reggae, outlaw country and power pop all belong precisely because the mix is incoherent. That incoherence IS the station.

Literal, not adjacent. 'Stoner rock' as a genre does not qualify a track -- Kyuss instrumentals, psychedelia, and 'good to smoke to' songs are the single most likely wrong proposal here. If you cannot quote the line, it does not go on.
One track per artist unless there is a real reason -- the roster is 28 songs about one subject and the same voice twice makes the joke feel thin rather than broad.
Innuendo and drug-general songs are out. 'Because I Got High' territory is fine; 'Purple Haze' (about a woman, whatever the myth says) and cocaine/pill songs are not, however famous.

rejections.reason: No such recording exists. Briefed 2026-08-26 as a literal weed track; every search resolves to "Stay Fly" (hook is "I gotta stay FLY", not about weed, so it fails this station's membership test) or to fan re-uploads that mislabel that same song "Stay High". "Da Summa" was offered as the genuine Three 6 weed track and declined -- the slot was dropped rather than filled, so the station currently carries no Memphis entry. Do not re-propose the title; it is not a recording.

rejections.track: Feel Good Hit of the Summer
rejections.reason: Fits the station perfectly on content (the chorus is a drug inventory naming marijuana first) and was still dropped, so it WILL look like an oversight later. The only official upload (QueensStoneAgeVEVO, bAXPUN2z2CE) is age-gated -- playabilityStatus LOGIN_REQUIRED, which the IFrame player cannot satisfy, so it would have been dead air. No Topic upload of the album track exists; Topic carries only the Reprise. Unofficial uploads were offered and declined. Re-propose only if a non-gated official source appears.
